nodes.label: Stacja B1 · 2
nodes.note: [B1 SPINE] PLACEHOLDER - end-of-level exit-velocity bank.

nodes.label: Ale, a, więc
nodes.note: First unit of B2. Seven invariable words the course never taught, all verified NEW: four joiners (ale, a, więc, albo) and three in-sentence particles (też, już, jeszcze). Zero morphology — none of them ever changes shape. The one teaching point, given its own slide and table, is i / a / ale: English collapses all three into and/but, Polish splits them by how the two halves relate. i (a2_past_plural) and bo (a2_questions2) are already-owned anchors, recycled as distractors, never re-taught. Two conservative scope cuts logged in the pack note: dlatego is left out (its partner dlatego że is on the C1 subordination list), and the negative-polarity readings już nie / jeszcze nie are fenced completely, since each flips its word's meaning rather than extending it.

nodes.label: Będę w domu
nodes.label_en: I will be… · the future of być
nodes.note: Pays the fork a2_bedzie took openly and logged in its own note: the copular future was not taught there, so 'I will be at home' was not expressible. It is now. Zero new forms and zero new lemmas — będę…będą have been owned since a2_bedzie and every complement type since A1. The whole payload is one syntactic fact: być is the only verb that never appears as an infinitive after będę, so będę stands alone and the complement follows it directly, in the slot it already occupies after jestem. Four complement types, all already owned: place, predicate adjective, Instrumental identity, and the impersonal adverb predicate (będzie dobrze — the future twin of a2_smalltalk's taught Było dobrze). a2_bedzie's 'the future has no gender' relief is explicitly preserved: the verb is one form, only the adjective after it agrees. Negation and the existential future are fenced (they govern the Genitive — deferred to b2_neg_gen), as are plural predicate adjectives, so every plural sentence here takes a place phrase.

nodes.label: Mamie, szkole, pracy
nodes.label_en: Feminine nouns · one form for Dative and Locative
nodes.note: Pays the item b1_dative_sg deferred by name: it handed mamie/tacie/siostrze over as memorised whole forms and logged that the general feminine dative/locative rule stayed untaught, for James to decide whether it needed a slot. This is that slot. THE GIFT, and the reason the unit earns its place: for feminine nouns the Dative and the Locative are the same form, so one rule pays for two cases — slide 1 is entirely this, with three nouns shown doing both jobs side by side. Light despite looking big: four of the nine forms drilled are already in the pool as one case each (mamie/siostrze as Datives, szkole/pracy as Locatives), so only kobiecie, łazience, ulicy, kuchni and sypialni are genuinely new. Two classes, both taught as visible closed families rather than a rule to run on an unseen noun: hard stem -a → -e with the consonant softening, and already-soft stem → -y/-i with nothing else changing. Teaching only the first class was the more conservative option and was rejected, because pracy is one of the most frequent forms in the course and would then sit in plain sight as a counterexample. tata is named in one line as the masculine -a noun that follows the same pattern (which is why the learner already says tacie) and is never drilled. Masculine datives, feminine accusatives and all plurals are fenced.

nodes.label: Dobrą kawę · biernik
nodes.label_en: Adjectives in the Accusative · only the feminine changes
nodes.note: B2 Block 2, unit 1 of 6 — the opening unit of the adjective-case block (spine O2), and deliberately the easiest of the six. IT ADDS NO NEW ENDING: a1_miec already taught the feminine swap in its own words (dobra kawa -> Mam dobrą kawę) and already stated the masculine-thing/neuter relief in its own body_pl (Męskie rzeczy i nijakie bez zmian). Verified with check_new.py: dobrą and nową are TAUGHT; małą, dużą, zimną, gorącą, starą, ładną are NEW. What is actually new is two small things — six more feminine object forms, each the same mechanical -a -> -ą on an adjective already owned in the Nominative, and the generalisation off mieć: a1_miec ran the pattern with one verb, this unit runs it after mam, piję, czytam, kupuję, kupię, robi and poproszę, which is what makes it a rule rather than a fact about having things. FENCED, and this is the fence most easily broken in this block: no oblique adjective endings (-ego, -ej, -ym, -emu) appear anywhere, not even as a quiz distractor, because b2_adj_gen is the very next unit. FENCED, second: masculine-animate accusative (dobrego psa) — named in one English line on slide 2 with no form shown; masculine animates appear in the pack only as grammatical subjects. No plural objects anywhere. Every recycled noun was re-checked for what it was taught AS (walizkę, pocztówkę, umowę, serwetkę, zupę, kawę, herbatę, wodę, książkę — all accusatives in their own packs); nowe and duże are deliberately unused, since a2_plural_nom taught them as PLURAL adjectives and using them as neuter singulars would spring that homograph unannounced.

nodes.label: Dobrej kawy · dopełniacz
nodes.note: B2 Block 2, unit 2 of 6 (spine O2) — the first unit of the block that adds real endings: -ego for masculine and neuter, -ej for feminine. FORM COUNT HELD DOWN ON PURPOSE: only four adjectives (dobry, nowy, mały, zimny), each in BOTH forms, so the learner sees a symmetrical paradigm rather than a word list. duży and stary were dropped for that reason alone and cost nothing to add later in a gym. Verified NEW: dobrego, dobrej, nowej, małego, małej, zimnego, zimnej. NO NEW GOVERNORS — all three triggers are already owned and are the ones the spine named: nie mam / nie ma + Gen, do + Gen, and dużo + Gen (a1_gen_endings literally teaches dużo kawy / dużo wody / dużo mleka). The only change is that the adjective now comes along. THE TRAP, predicted by spine O16 one batch in advance and confirmed here: nowego reports TAUGHT (a2_smalltalk) but is frozen inside the chunk Nic nowego. Slide 3 is entirely that reveal, played as a gift rather than a correction — the dziękuję / której precedent. MASCULINE-ANIMATE ACCUSATIVE folds in here and closes the gap b2_adj_acc left open by design one unit earlier: for masculine people and animals the object form IS this form (Mam małego psa), and the nouns have been Acc=Gen since a1_miec. That pairing is the whole reason these two units sit in this order. FENCED: z / ze + Genitive is kept out entirely, even though it is an owned Genitive governor, because inserting an adjective flips the learner's whole-form ze sklepu back to z nowego sklepu — a second fact about the preposition, not the adjective, and the do/z cliff in miniature. Also fenced: -ym and -emu anywhere including distractors; plural genitive adjectives (C1); and pracy, which b2_fem_soft taught one unit earlier as the Dative/Locative form. Distractors are real taught forms in the wrong slot, including last unit's accusatives (dobrą, nową, małą, zimną); zimne and stare are avoided as both came back NEW and are taught nowhere.

nodes.label: Praca i biuro
nodes.note: B2 Block 2 vocab interleave, placed so the six-unit adjective block is not six grammar units in a row and so the two adjective cases just taught get a pack of real sentences to breathe in. All twelve words re-verified NEW with check_new.py at build time rather than trusted from the spine (wynagrodzenie, zwolnienie, nadgodziny, obowiązek, stanowisko, podanie, rozmowa, zatrudnienie, wykształcenie, kwalifikacje, etat, raport), and all thirteen spine anchors re-verified TAUGHT and recycled, never re-taught. THE GIFT: eleven of the twelve need no second form — six neuter, three masculine things and two non-virile plurals all have an object form identical to the plain form, so only rozmowa takes one (rozmowę, the -a/-ę swap owned since a1_miec). Twelve words, one extra form. ROZMOWA IS A CHUNK-TO-WORD REVEAL: check_new.py calls the bare word new, but a2_work2 taught rozmowa kwalifikacyjna as one frozen lump a level ago; the gloss names the plain word and the bank uses only that sense. A SENSE WAS CUT ON PURPOSE: zwolnienie is glossed only as dismissal — the sick-note sense (zwolnienie lekarskie) appears nowhere and belongs to b2_health_system later in this same block-list. FEEDS b2_verbal_nouns and deliberately does not spend it: five of these words are -enie/-anie verbal nouns, and nothing here names the verb behind any of them or mentions the pattern. FENCED, the easy one to break in a vocab pack: adjectives appear only in Nominative, Accusative and Genitive — never inside a Locative or Instrumental phrase (no nowym biurze), because -ym is two units away. Every place phrase takes a bare noun. No genitive forms of the new nouns either; the two genitive sentences use already-owned biura so the new adjective ending drills without a new noun ending riding along.

nodes.label: W nowej pracy · miejscownik
nodes.label_en: Adjectives in the Locative · -ym, and -ej again
nodes.note: B2 Block 2, unit 3 of 6 (spine O2). ONE new ending: -ym for masculine and neuter. The feminine -ej is the form b2_adj_gen taught one unit ago, unchanged — so the whole unit is FOUR NEW FORMS: dobrym, nowym, małym, zimnym (all verified NEW). Same four adjectives as b2_adj_gen on purpose, so the block reads as one paradigm widening rather than a growing word list. THE CENTRAL CONTRAST, and the reason the unit can be this small: Genitive and Locative disagree about which word moves, and they disagree in opposite directions by gender. Feminine — the adjective is the same in both and the noun is not (do dobrej szkoły vs w dobrej szkole). Masculine like dom — the noun is the same in both (domu either way) and only the adjective marks the difference (do nowego domu vs w nowym domu). That minimal pair is slide 4 and the Kontrola stage is built on it; it is also why this unit sits immediately after b2_adj_gen. NO NEW GOVERNORS: w and na (a1_prep_place, a1_prep_review_1/2, a2_house) and o (a2_o_loc, which supplies o domu / o sklepie / o pracy / o banku wholesale) — all re-checked as whole chunks rather than assumed. A SPINE EXAMPLE HAD TO BE REJECTED: B2-SPINE's own illustration for this unit was 'Myślę o dobrym filmie', but filmie reports NEW (the course owns film, filmy, filmów and has never inflected it); wodzie, mleku, samochodzie and restauracji are NEW for the same reason. The unit runs on attested Locative noun forms only. FENCED: -emu appears nowhere including as a distractor (b2_adj_dat owns it, two units away); no plural oblique adjectives (C1, spine O3); nowe and duże are used nowhere at all despite reporting TAUGHT, because a2_plural_nom taught them as PLURALS — the neuter singular slots take dobre and małe instead, holding b2_adj_acc's standing line; zimne and stare are NEW and appear nowhere. Distractors are real taught Polish in the wrong slot: last unit's Genitives (nowego, małego, dobrego, zimnego) and the Accusatives from two units back (nową, małą, dobrą, zimną), which makes every wrong choice a genuine near-miss rather than noise.

nodes.label: Dobrym nauczycielem · narzędnik
nodes.label_en: Adjectives in the Instrumental · no new endings
nodes.note: B2 Block 2, unit 4 of 6 (spine O2). ZERO new endings and ZERO new lemmas — the whole unit is already-owned material doing a job it has not done before. All six adjective forms report TAUGHT: dobrym, nowym, małym <- b2_adj_loc one unit ago; dobrą, nową <- a1_miec [path 9]; małą <- b2_adj_acc. Masculine and neuter reuse the -ym of the Locative, feminine reuses the -ą the learner has had as an object form since his ninth unit. teaches_lemmas is empty, which is legitimate and precedented — b2_copular_future is the same shape, and the auditor only warns when BOTH teaches_* are empty. THE FOURTH TURN OF THE COURSE'S SIGNATURE IDIOM: inst_identity → inst_z → inst_transport → here, each time the endings staying and the job changing; this unit adds the adjective to all three jobs at once rather than inventing a fourth. WHY IT EARNS A SLOT rather than folding into b2_adj_loc — the discrimination it adds is invisible from either unit alone: for masculine and neuter the Locative and Instrumental adjective are the SAME form (w dobrym hotelu / z dobrym kolegą), but for feminine they DIFFER (w dobrej firmie / z dobrą siostrą), so gender decides whether the two cases can be told apart at all. Slide 4 is that table and quiz item 8 tests it. SECOND POINT, one line and one table row: kolega is a masculine noun whose Instrumental ends in -ą, so z dobrym kolegą pairs a masculine adjective with an -ą noun. The learner has owned kolegą since a2_inst_z and kolega's masculinity since A1; putting an adjective in front of it is the first moment that masculinity is visible on the page — a gift, not a load, but stated explicitly because a Match board showing z dobrym kolegą beside z małą siostrą would otherwise look self-contradictory. FENCED: -emu appears nowhere including as a distractor (b2_adj_dat is the very next unit); no plural oblique adjectives (C1, spine O3); zimny is left out entirely because none of the Instrumental's three jobs has a natural home for 'cold' and wodą is NEW anyway — costless, since the unit teaches no forms; starym and dużym are NEW and appear nowhere, which is why starym samochodem, the most idiomatic transport phrase in the language, could not be used; nowe and duże remain unused, holding b2_adj_acc's standing line about a2_plural_nom's plurals. B2-SPINE'S OWN EXAMPLE FOR THIS UNIT WAS REJECTED: 'Jadę z miłą siostrą' — miłą reports NEW. That is the second spine example in this batch to fail check_new.py; b2_adj_loc's 'Myślę o dobrym filmie' was the first.

nodes.label: Dobremu · celownik
nodes.label_en: Adjectives in the Dative · -emu, and -ej a third time
nodes.note: B2 Block 2, unit 5 of 6 (spine O2) — the last teaching unit of the adjective block, and small by design exactly as the spine said. THREE NEW FORMS: dobremu, nowemu, małemu. The feminine -ej is recycled for the THIRD time (Genitive, Locative, now Dative), which is what slide 2 is built on: dobrej has quietly become the busiest adjective form the learner owns. GOVERNORS all owned and all used — pomagać and dziękować from b1_dative_sg, dawać from b1_giving, which is where b1_dative_sg's own logged deferral of that verb was paid ('do not assume dawać is already covered' — it is, since path 119, and this was re-checked rather than assumed). DATIVE NOUNS: studentowi, nauczycielowi, bratu, siostrze, mamie (b1_dative_sg) and kobiecie (b2_fem_soft); homograph check performed on all six and every one is reused in exactly the slot it was taught in. THE ONE REAL JUDGMENT CALL — NEUTER IS STATED BUT NOT DRILLED: dziecku reports NEW and is the only plausible neuter Dative noun in reach, so the course owns NO neuter noun in this case. Rather than bolt a new noun form onto a unit already adding an ending, the neuter is named in one English line and given its column in the recap table — true, consistent with every other oblique case in the block, and demanding no unmet form. If James wants it drilled, dziecku is the single form to add and małemu dziecku is the phrase. CLOSES THE BLOCK: b2_adj_gym is next and teaches nothing, so slide 4 is a six-row recap of the adjective across all four cases in three genders — every cell checked individually, all forms taught at or before this point. KONTROLA CARRIES THE BLOCK'S PAYOFF: items 6 and 7 are cross-case discriminations against the Genitive (Nie mam dobrego brata) and the Instrumental (Jestem dobrym studentem) — the first time the learner must choose among four oblique adjective forms rather than two. All ten quiz answers distinct. FENCED: zimny left out for the second unit running (no Dative recipient is cold, and zimnemu would be a fourth new form bought for nothing); nowej and zimnej unused too, since two feminine examples make the -ej point and more would pad a unit whose whole virtue is being small; nowe and duże still unused anywhere, holding b2_adj_acc's standing line; no plural obliques (C1, spine O3).

nodes.label: Siłownia · dobry
nodes.label_en: Adjective gym · every case, one adjective
nodes.note: B2 Block 2, unit 6 of 6 (spine O2) — the gym that closes the adjective block. Gym idiom (a1_case_gym / a2_case_gym2 / b1_case_gym / b1_virile_gym line): ZERO new material, teaches_structures and teaches_lemmas both EMPTY. WHAT THE GYM ADDS THAT NO SINGLE UNIT COULD: the block taught the adjective one case at a time, so the learner has never seen the collisions. Slide 2 is the whole point — dobrej does THREE jobs (Genitive, Locative, Dative, feminine), dobrym does TWO (Locative and Instrumental, m/n), dobrą does TWO (Accusative and Instrumental, feminine), dobrego does TWO (Genitive, and the object form of a masculine animate). The line the slide lands: the ending alone does not name the job — the verb or preposition in front of it does. KONTROLA ITEMS 6 AND 7 ARE DELIBERATELY THE SAME FOUR CHOICES (nowego/nowym/nowemu/nowy) under two different sentences, Idę do ___ sklepu versus Mieszkam w ___ domu — the cleanest demonstration that the sentence decides, since nothing else about the two items differs (b1_case_gym's paired ci/te idiom). All 12 quiz answers distinct, achieved by varying the adjective rather than the job. ZIMNY EVENED UP, partially and honestly: B2-DIGEST batch 3 flagged that zimny dropped out of the block after b2_adj_loc, so this gym puts zimną (Acc), zimnej (Gen and Loc) and zimnym (Loc) back in real slots; it does NOT reach zimnemu, which is taught nowhere in the course, so the Dative of zimny stays out, distractors included. HOMOGRAPH CHECKS on every recycled form: kawy is used only as a Genitive singular (a1_gen_endings), never as the nominative plural AGENTS.md names as the trap; nowego is used only in the real Genitive sense b2_adj_gen re-taught, not a2_smalltalk's frozen nic nowego; mamie and siostrze are Datives, as b1_dative_sg taught them; brata and psa are the masculine-animate Acc=Gen exception, named in its own slide row rather than slipped past; mamy appears nowhere. FENCED: nowe and duże appear nowhere including as distractors (a2_plural_nom taught both as PLURALS — b2_adj_acc's standing line, held for six units running); zimne is NEW and appears nowhere; no plural oblique adjectives anywhere (C1, spine O3); no oblique pronouns (go, ją, cię, nim, niej) since b2_pron_acc and b2_pron_prep are the next two units — a fence the auditor cannot see at all, because person pronouns sit in audit.py's GLUE_LEMMAS.

nodes.label: Kocham cię · biernik
nodes.label_en: Object pronouns · the other half of mi, ci, mu
nodes.note: B2 Block 3, unit 1 (spine). SIX NEW FORMS: cię, go, ją, nas, was, ich — all verified NEW at build time; mnie reports TAUGHT and is the seventh, re-taught explicitly here. THE UNIT PAYS AN IOU THREE LEVELS OLD, and that is why it exists: a2_dat_chunks taught boli mnie as a frozen block and its own note says 'mnie in boli mnie is accusative, not dative — deliberately NOT explained'; b1_dative_pron then refused to generalise boleć onto the new dative pronouns and said why ('it takes the accusative in every person, a different pronoun set the course has not taught… this unit does not touch that fence'). The course now has that set, so the fence comes down here and nowhere earlier, and boli is finally run across persons (boli mnie / boli cię / boli go). THE GIFT, and slide 2: half the table is already owned — the Dative column (mi, ci, mu, jej, nam, wam, im) has been complete since path 118, so this is one new column beside one the learner already has, not fourteen new words. The verb decides the column and slide 3 is that list, using only verbs already owned on both sides. WORD ORDER, one line and a real fence: every item puts the object pronoun immediately after its verb, and where the pronoun is a short clitic (cię, go, ją, mi, ci, mu, jej) the verb is also clause-initial — Kocham cię, Lubię go, Pomagam mu, Boli mnie głowa — which is always natural. Noun-subject sentences use only the full forms (Mama zna nas, Tata lubi was), because Mama kocha cię is marked where Mama cię kocha is neutral, and choosing between them is a word-order fact, not a pronoun fact; stated to the learner as the same rule się already has since a2_sie, and the fuller story left where B2-SPINE's C1 list already puts it. FENCED: ALL n- forms after prepositions (niego, niej, nim, nich, nimi) appear nowhere, not in a slide and not as a distractor — b2_pron_prep is the very next unit and owns them, and this fence is NOT machine-enforced, because person pronouns sit in audit.py's GLUE_LEMMAS; it was checked by hand over every learner-facing string. Also fenced: je (neuter and non-virile-plural accusative), both because the virile split arriving in a new place is a second fact and because it collides with je 'he/she eats' — consequence stated openly, 'them' is expressible only for people until C1; the long emphatic forms jego and ciebie; siebie/sobie (C1, spine O15); and negated objects anywhere, since nie znam jej would put the object in the Genitive, which is b2_neg_gen's job later in this level. ADVANCE WARNING, in the b1_virile_reco tradition: ich is also the possessive 'their'. Only mój and twój are taught, so there is no collision today, but whichever unit extends the possessives will be re-teaching this exact string as an unrelated word and should expect the ci/ci treatment. SECOND WARNING, cross-language and not covered by the homograph table: was is an English word, and a learner reading an English prompt can read the Polish was as the English verb — named in the explain on its own quiz item rather than left to sting. ci appears only in its Dative sense; its virile-demonstrative sense appears nowhere, deliberately, since cię and ci are already a one-letter minimal pair carrying the unit's central contrast. All 12 quiz answers distinct.

nodes.label: Znam go · do niego
nodes.label_en: Pronouns after a preposition · they all start with n-
nodes.note: B2 Block 3, unit 2 (spine). SIX NEW FORMS: niego, niej, nim, nią, nich, nimi — all verified NEW. PAYS a2_o_loc's NAMED FENCE, which said in its own note: 'pronoun objects — o tobie, o mnie, o nim, o niej are new pronoun forms, absent from POOL, and are never shown, glossed or demanded… They need their own small unit.' This is that unit, for the third person. THE WHOLE RULE IS ONE LINE: after a preposition, the him/her/them pronouns all start with n-. The three governors are the three already owned and each keeps the case it has always had — o + Locative, z + Instrumental, do + Genitive — so nothing about the prepositions changes; a clean 3x3 grid with only six distinct shapes in it. THE GIFT, slide 2: the pronoun collapses its cases in exactly the pattern the adjective block just taught — nim covers Locative and Instrumental for masculine precisely as dobrym does (w dobrym hotelu / z dobrym kolegą), and niej covers Genitive and Locative for feminine precisely as dobrej does (do dobrej szkoły / w dobrej firmie). Naming that parallel costs nothing and turns six forms into three plus a pattern already owned. THE ONE REAL JUDGMENT CALL, conservative branch taken — THIRD PERSON ONLY: o mnie, o tobie, ze mną, z tobą, do ciebie, z nami, z wami appear nowhere, because tobie, tobą, mną, ciebie, nami and wami are all verified NEW (six more forms) and ze mną additionally needs the ze-shape of z before m + consonant, which is a fact about the PREPOSITION, not the pronoun — the do/z cliff in miniature. The tempting middle option was rejected on purpose: o mnie, o nas and o was would cost zero new strings (all three were taught one unit ago), but shipping them without o tobie would leave the most frequent cell of the row missing, and a half-row whose hole is the useful cell is worse than a clean fence. THE ALTERNATIVE if James wants it: a small follow-up unit with those six forms plus the ze-rule, or folding them in here at the cost of doubling the unit. dla WAS DROPPED — B2-SPINE's own illustrative example for this unit is 'do niego, dla niej', but dla reports NEW: a preposition the course has never taught, so using it would smuggle a new governor into a pronoun unit. This is batch 3's finding repeating — the spine is a design document, not a pool. niemu is not taught either, for a cleaner reason: no preposition in this course governs the Dative, so the form would have no legal sentence to sit in. w/na + pronoun fenced too, since w nim would put nim into a third job inside the unit that introduces it. THE RISK THE UNIT IS BUILT AROUND: the learner has owned go, ją and ich for exactly one unit, and the wrong sentence is 'do go' rather than 'do niego' — so every bare-form / n-form pair is drilled against itself (quiz 1 vs 7, 2 vs 8, 5 vs 9, with mu/jej/im as third options), and Match rows 10-12 deliberately put the three bare object forms on the same board as their n- partners. FENCED, held from b2_pron_acc: je and nie, jego, ciebie, siebie/sobie (C1, spine O15), and negated objects anywhere. None of this is machine-enforced — person pronouns sit in audit.py's GLUE_LEMMAS, so every pronoun fence in this block was checked by hand, string by string, over every learner-facing surface. All 12 quiz answers distinct.

nodes.label: Kto? Kogo? Z kim?
nodes.note: B2 Block 3, unit 3 (spine). FIVE NEW FORMS: kogo, czego, komu, kim, czym — all verified NEW. kto and co both report TAUGHT (a1_questions) and are the anchors, recycled and never re-taught. PAYS TWO NAMED FENCES AT ONCE, which is why the spine gave it a slot. (1) a2_inst_z's: 'kim is a new pronoun form and is not in POOL; if James wants Z kim? as a live question it needs its own small unit.' That fence is also the reason one of AGENTS.md's three named title-rule violations exists (the old 'Z kim?' title carrying an untaught form). (2) a2_o_loc's: o czym was kept out of every slide AND out of body_pl there. Both are paid here, in the same five forms. THE FRAME: kto and co have been subjects since A1 (Kto to jest? Co to jest?). Put either one anywhere else in the sentence and it takes a case, exactly like a noun or an adjective, and exactly the same governor decides which — the verb or the preposition in front of it. No new governors anywhere in this unit: object verbs (miec_acc, pron_acc's verb list), do + Genitive (prep_do_gen), nie ma + Genitive (negation), pomagać/dziękować + Dative (dative_sg), o + Locative (o_loc), z + Instrumental (inst_z), bare Instrumental of transport (inst_transport), and być + Instrumental identity (inst_identity). THE GIFT, and slide 2 — the forms collapse in patterns the learner has met twice in the last five units. kogo does the object job AND the do / nie ma job, which is not a new idea at all: b2_adj_gen taught exactly that merger for masculine people and animals (Mam małego psa / do małego psa), and kto is a person, so it behaves like one. kim and czym each cover Locative and Instrumental, precisely as nim does (b2_pron_prep, one unit ago) and precisely as dobrym does (b2_adj_loc / b2_adj_inst). So five forms carry eight jobs and only three of the mergers have to be learned, because all three are re-sightings. THE HONEST CONTRAST that keeps the learner from over-applying it: for a THING the object form is just co (Co masz?), because things never do the Acc-equals-Gen merger. czego is the do / nie ma form only. This is one line and one quiz pair (items 1 and 10). czemu IS FENCED AND APPEARS NOWHERE — not in a table, not as a distractor. Two reasons, either sufficient: the Dative of a thing is rare enough that this learner gets no value from it, and czemu is also colloquial Polish for 'why', so shipping it here would plant a homograph in the same unit that introduces the form. The Dative row of the table therefore carries an em dash in the thing column, and the slide says plainly that things almost never take that one. INDIRECT QUESTIONS ARE FENCED ABSOLUTELY. Every kim / czym / kogo / czego / komu in this pack is a DIRECT question with a question mark. Nie wiem, kogo znasz appears nowhere — embedded questions are b2_indirect_q's single new fact, four units later on the path, and a2_questions2 already fenced them by name ('no indirect questions: Nie wiem, kiedy... is B1'). QUIZ ANSWER REPEATS ARE DELIBERATE, and this is the b2_adj_gym precedent stated again. The unit has exactly seven legal answer strings (kto, co, kogo, czego, komu, kim, czym), so twelve distinct quiz answers is arithmetically impossible without padding or fabrication. Instead the quiz is built on FIVE MINIMAL PAIRS — items 1/2 (kogo as object vs kogo after do), 4/5 (komu after two different Dative verbs), 6/7 (kim after o vs after z), 8/9 (czym after o vs bare for transport), 1/10 (kogo for a person vs co for a thing). Two items carrying the same answer under two different sentences is the cleanest possible demonstration that the sentence decides the form, which is the whole unit; b2_adj_gym made the same call for the same reason. No two prompts are the same. FENCED: czemu (above); czyj (NEW); kim/czym in any plural or after any preposition other than o and z; na/za/dla + question word (dla itself reports NEW and was already dropped from b2_pron_prep for that reason); negated objects anywhere, held from b2_pron_acc, since Nie znam kogo would need the Genitive of negation, which is b2_neg_gen's job later in this level; and Kogo nie ma? — deliberately not shown even though it is grammatical, because it puts a person into the nie ma slot the pack has just used for things, one contrast too many. WORD-ORDER NOTE: every question here puts the question word first, which is the only order taught and the only one used. Noun subjects sit after the verb (O kim mówi tata?), which is the neutral order for a wh-question and matches how b1_ktory_cases already writes them. Distractors are real taught Polish in the wrong slot throughout — every wrong choice is another form from this same unit, or kto/co, doing a job it does not do. Nothing fabricated. Bare governed prepositions (o, z, do) are not listed in uses_lemmas per SEQUENCING.md 6.3 — their jobs ride o_loc, inst_z and prep_do_gen, all declared in uses_structures.

nodes.label: Przychodnia i szpital
nodes.note: B2 Block 3 vocab (spine). TWELVE NEW WORDS, all verified NEW: skierowanie, leczenie, objaw, diagnoza, oddział, pogotowie, zabieg, operacja, specjalista, rejestracja, wyniki, izba przyjęć. THE REGISTER IS THE SYSTEM, NOT THE BODY. a1_body, leaf_health_a1 and a2_health2 already own symptoms-as-body-parts, medicines and how you feel; this pack is about NAVIGATING CARE — the referral, the desk you check in at, the ward, the results, the emergency entrance. ANCHORS, recycled and never re-taught: lekarz, pacjent, wizyta, karetka, pielęgniarka (leaf_health_a1), ubezpieczenie, recepta, badanie, przychodnia, szczepienie (a2_health2), kolejka (leaf_shopping_a1), szpital (leaf_places), termin (b1_plans). izba przyjęć IS TAUGHT AS ONE FROZEN CHUNK, and this is the pack's main judgment call, made deliberately and logged. B2-SPINE lists the candidate as bare izba, but izba on its own is a near-archaic word for a room and would be a misleading thing to hand this learner; izba przyjęć is the sign actually on the hospital door and is what he would need to read. The genitive plural inside it (przyjęć) is NOT taught, NOT explained and NOT decomposed — the gloss says to learn it whole. This follows the established multiword-citation precedent already live in the course: piłka nożna, w porządku (a1_freetime), dom handlowy, rozmowa kwalifikacyjna, praca domowa, zwrot pieniędzy, nauki ścisłe. The alternative was to drop it for a simpler single word (zastrzyk and dyżur were both checked and are NEW and available); rejected because it would leave the spine's own slot unpaid and lose the highest real-life-value item in the set. specjalista IS A MASCULINE NOUN ENDING IN -a, the exact trap AGENTS.md names ('watch soft feminines and -a masculines'). Its gender badge says m, and sentence 15's explain points at the two -a masculines the learner has owned since A1, tata and kolega, rather than asserting the gender flatly. It is never given an adjective in the feminine, and its accusative specjalistę is NOT taught — that form is irregular enough to need its own moment and earns nothing here. FOUR INFLECTED FORMS ARE TAUGHT ALONGSIDE THEIR CITATION FORMS, per AGENTS.md's every-form-taught rule and the b2_work precedent (rozmowa / rozmowę): objawy (plural, the ordinary -y of plural_nom), diagnozę and operację (feminine accusative, the -a to -ę swap owned since a1_miec), and skierowania (genitive). skierowania IS THE ONE FORM THAT EXTENDS A RULE, and it is handed over whole rather than derived. gen_endings states the neuter genitive as -o to -a (okno to okna); skierowanie is a neuter in -e, and -e neuters take -a as well. That is the same landing point by the same logic, but the course has never shown an -e neuter in the genitive, so the form is taught as a memorised whole with an explain that names what it is doing, exactly the treatment kelnerzy, mógłby and the family datives received. It earns this because Nie mam skierowania is the single most useful sentence in the pack. FLAGGED FOR JAMES: if he would rather the course stayed silent on -e neuter genitives until a rule unit, sentence 3 is the only place to remove and nothing else depends on it. FENCED: na + Accusative appears nowhere, which cost two obvious sentences (dzwonię na pogotowie, czekam na wyniki) — na has only ever been a Locative preposition in this course (prep_w_loc) and na + Acc would be a new governor smuggled in through a vocab leaf. Oblique forms of the new nouns beyond the four listed above appear nowhere: no oddziale, rejestracji, leczeniu, wyników, zabiegu. No plural obliques. Indirect questions appear nowhere (b2_indirect_q owns them). Sentence bank spreads across 24 already-owned structures, including question_cases from the unit immediately before this one on the path.

nodes.label: Stacja B2 · 1
nodes.note: [B2 SPINE] PLACEHOLDER - rep bank. Stays 'planned' forever, same as A2's four stations and B1's two. Never authored, never flipped live.

nodes.label: Wiem, że…
nodes.note: B2 Block 4, unit 1 (spine). ZERO NEW LEMMAS. The unit's entire content is a joint: że as a productive conjunction attaching a whole sentence to a verb of knowing or saying. CHUNK-TO-PARADIGM REVEAL, and B2-SPINE O16 predicted it a block in advance. że reports TAUGHT (b1_polite) but only frozen inside Przepraszam, że przeszkadzam — b1_polite's own note says 'że and przeszkadzam both verified untaught... never built'. It is re-taught here explicitly as a real word with a real job, and the slide says so out loud: you already say this word, you have just never used it like this. Same treatment b1_dative_sg gave dziękuję, b1_ktory_cases gave której, b2_adj_gen gave nowego and b2_pron_acc gave mnie. Per the b2_adj_gen precedent an already-owned string stays in uses_lemmas rather than teaches_lemmas, so teaches_lemmas is legitimately empty (the copular_future / adj_inst precedent). wiem IS A SECOND CHUNK-TO-SLOT REVEAL, and it carries a hard fence with it. a2_directions_func taught wiem as a street phrase and quarantined it in its own note: 'this unit NEVER mentions znam, never conjugates wiem, and never shows the infinitive.' That quarantine is HELD here — wiem appears only in the first person, and wiesz, wie and wiedzieć appear nowhere, all three being NEW and the wiedzieć-versus-znać split being live untaught ground. Nie wiem, że is also absent, and not only for that reason: negated wiedzieć takes czy or a question word in real Polish, and that is an indirect question, which is fenced below. THE DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE SPINE BRIEF, taken on the conservative branch and logged. B2-SPINE says this unit rides 'mówił/mówiła (a2_past_rest)'. It does not: EVERY matrix verb here is present tense (wiem, myślę, myślisz, mówię, mówisz, mówi). Reason: the moment a past-tense verb of saying takes a że-clause, the learner meets the fact that Polish does not back-shift the tense (Powiedział, że jest zmęczony), and that fact is b2_reported's ONE new idea, on the very next node of the path. Handing it over early, unnamed, inside a unit about a conjunction would spend b2_reported's whole payoff to save nothing. Keeping the matrix present-tense also removes the mówił glossing problem entirely (AGENTS.md's dynamic-verb rule would force 'was saying', which reads oddly in a reporting frame). Nothing in b2_reported depends on this choice being reversed. THE COMMA IS THE SECOND FACT, and it is one line: Polish always writes a comma before że, and never drops że itself. English does the opposite on both counts — 'I know she is at home' has no comma and no 'that'. That asymmetry is exactly why an English speaker under-produces both, so it is named rather than left to be absorbed. THE że / żeby DISCRIMINATION IS INCLUDED, and it adds no new material — both words are owned (b1_zeby taught żeby for purpose and for want-that). They are a one-letter-plus pair now sitting in the same syntactic slot, so confusing them is the predictable error, and the b1_two_futures idiom is the house answer to exactly this shape of problem. The line the unit lands: że reports what is so; żeby says why you are doing something or what you want someone else to do. Match row 12 and quiz items 2, 7 and 12 carry it. THE że / który DISCRIMINATION IS THE OTHER HALF, and it is arguably the more valuable one, because the confusion is caused by ENGLISH rather than by Polish: English 'that' is both the conjunction and the relative pronoun, so 'I know that...' and 'the book that I read' look identical to this learner while Polish keeps them completely separate (że versus który/którą, b1_ktory_cases). Quiz items 3 and 9 are that pair, and both reuse b1_ktory_cases' own example sentences rather than inventing new ones. QUIZ ANSWER REPEATS ARE DELIBERATE, same reasoning as b2_kim_czym one batch ago: a unit about one conjunction has few legal answer strings. Five distinct answers (że, żeby, który, którą, bo) across twelve items, every prompt distinct, and the repeats of że are all under structurally different sentences. FENCED: all past-tense matrix verbs (above); INDIRECT QUESTIONS ABSOLUTELY — no czy, gdzie, kiedy, ile, dlaczego or any question word after a matrix verb anywhere in this pack, because that is b2_indirect_q's single new fact two nodes later and a2_questions2 fenced it by name ('no indirect questions: Nie wiem, kiedy... is B1'); wiesz / wie / wiedzieć; mam nadzieję (nadzieję verified NEW), cieszę się, uważam and wydaje mi się (uważam and wydaje mi się are b2_discussion_func's material, at the end of the level); słyszę, że — słyszę is a frozen phone chunk (a2_phone_func teaches only Nie słyszę) and putting it in front of a clause would be a third chunk-to-slot reveal in one unit; object pronouns anywhere, because an object clitic inside a subordinate clause raises word-order questions b2_pron_acc explicitly left to C1. Distractors are real taught Polish in the wrong slot throughout — every wrong choice is że, żeby, bo, i, ale, który or którą, each a conjunction or pronoun the learner owns, placed where it does not belong. Nothing fabricated.

nodes.label: Powiedział, że…
nodes.note: B2 Block 4, unit 2 (spine). ONE NEW WORD (powiedzieć, handed over whole in five forms) and ONE NEW FACT: Polish does not back-shift the tense. Whatever tense the speaker actually used is the tense you keep when you report them, so English 'Dad said the shop WAS closed' is Polish Tata powiedział, że sklep JEST zamknięty. Framed as a gift, the a2_bedzie 'the future has no gender' idiom: this is one fewer thing to do than English, not one more. THE UNIT INHERITS A CLEAN SLATE AND SPENDS IT ON EXACTLY ONE THING. b2_ze_clauses one node earlier deliberately kept every matrix verb in the present tense and logged why: the instant a past-tense verb of saying takes a że-clause the learner meets the no-back-shift fact, and that fact belongs here. That deferral is now cashed in. The joint itself (matrix + comma + że + untouched clause) is therefore entirely owned material, and the only thing this pack adds on top of it is the past-tense matrix verb. powiedzieć IS TAUGHT AS THE PERFECTIVE TWIN OF THE OWNED mówić, whole, per B2-SPINE O7.2's closed-list treatment and a2_aspect's standing framing (the prefixes are unpredictable; learn the pair whole, never build the second verb from the first). powiedzieć is not even prefixed — it is a suppletive partner — which makes it the honest kind of pair for that rule rather than a counterexample to it. Five forms taught: powiedzieć, powiedziałem, powiedziałam, powiedział, powiedziała. The gender split is not a new fact, just past_ac applied to a new verb, and it is presented that way. GLOSSING, per AGENTS.md's dynamic-verb rule. powiedzieć is perfective and glosses as plain 'said' — one completed act of speech, no ambiguity. mówić is imperfective and dynamic, so wherever mówił/mówiła appears it is glossed 'was saying' or 'kept saying', never 'said'. That is precisely the pair contrast slide 3 teaches, and it is why b2_ze_clauses' note flagged 'was saying' as reading oddly in a reporting frame: it reads oddly only when it is doing the job of 'said', and here it never is. THE PERSON SHIFT IS FENCED, and this is the unit's one real judgment call, taken on the conservative branch. No item anywhere asks the learner to turn a quoted Jestem zmęczony into a reported jest zmęczony. Every intro transformation shows a quote whose subject is a noun (Sklep jest zamknięty → Tata powiedział, że sklep jest zamknięty), so literally nothing inside the clause moves and the no-back-shift message lands uncluttered. Where a report does come out third-person (Tata powiedział, że jest zmęczony) it is only ever driven from an English prompt that already says 'he', so the learner is never performing a person transformation, only a translation. THE ARGUMENT FOR THE OTHER BRANCH IS REAL AND IS RECORDED HERE: the person shift is not a Polish-specific fact at all — English does the identical shift — so including it would arguably cost no new learning. It was still left out because it is extra production work inside the unit that introduces the tense fact, and load-splitting decides ties in this course. If James wants it, it is a slide and three items, not a rewrite. FENCED, all verified and deliberate: PLURAL past of both verbs — powiedzieli, powiedziały and mówili are all verified NEW strings and would add virile forms to a unit that is about tense, so every matrix verb here is singular; the non-past forms of powiedzieć (powiem, powiesz — verified NEW), which are perfective FUTURE and would put a second tense job on the new word; wiedzieć, wiesz and wie, still held under a2_directions_func's quarantine that b2_ze_clauses restated (wiem appears here not at all, since the openers are all verbs of saying); INDIRECT QUESTIONS ABSOLUTELY — no question word after any matrix verb anywhere in this pack, not in a prompt, not as a distractor, because that is b2_indirect_q's single new fact on the very next node and a2_questions2 fenced it by name; masculine-ANIMATE relative pronouns (którego with a person antecedent), which is b2_ktory_full's material two nodes later, so the one który item here keeps b1_ktory_cases' inanimate antecedent; pamiętam (verified NEW), which would have been the obvious second matrix verb and is simply not owned. DISTRACTORS ARE REAL TAUGHT POLISH IN THE WRONG SLOT throughout. The tense items are guarded with był/była/miała/miałem — genuine past forms the learner owns since A2, which is what makes the choice a real discrimination rather than a spelling test: the wrong answer is exactly what an English speaker would produce by back-shifting. The gender items are guarded with the other three forms of powiedzieć taught in this same pack. Nothing fabricated anywhere. QUIZ ANSWER REPEATS: none — twelve items, twelve distinct answers, which a unit with four new forms plus a tense contrast can afford (b2_ze_clauses could not, and said so).

nodes.label: Nie wiem, gdzie…
nodes.label_en: Putting a question inside a sentence
nodes.note: B2 Block 4, unit 3 (spine). ZERO NEW LEMMAS — every question word is owned, and so is czy. The unit is a joint plus one re-sighting, exactly like b2_ze_clauses two nodes back, and it pays a2_questions2's fence by name: that pack's own note says 'no indirect questions (Nie wiem, kiedy... is B1)'. Never built at B1; built here. THE HEADLINE IS A GIFT, not a rule — the third unit in a row that takes something away rather than adding it (b2_copular_future, b2_reported, this). English REORDERS a question when it goes inside a bigger sentence: 'Where IS the chemist's?' becomes 'I don't know where the chemist's IS'. Polish never inverted in the first place, so there is nothing to undo. The question goes in exactly as it stands, after a comma. This is stated as the slide-1 headline because it is the whole reason the construction is easy, and because an English speaker will otherwise expect to have to do something and go looking for it. THE ONE NEW JOB is czy meaning 'whether' / 'if'. czy is owned since a1_questions as the marker on a yes-or-no question (Czy jest chleb?), and the honest framing — used on slide 2 — is that it is doing the SAME job in the SAME way, just inside a bigger sentence rather than alone. The asymmetry worth naming is on the English side: English switches to a different word ('whether', 'if') where Polish simply keeps czy. Chunk-to-slot extension, the dziękuję / której / nowego / mnie / że precedent, so per the b2_adj_gen convention czy stays in uses_lemmas and teaches_lemmas is legitimately empty (copular_future / adj_inst / ze_clauses precedent). THE że / czy MINIMAL PAIR IS THE SHARPEST THING IN THE UNIT and costs no new material: Wiem, że mama jest w domu versus Nie wiem, czy mama jest w domu — the same clause, and the opener alone decides whether you are reporting something settled or leaving it open. Quiz items 3 and 4 are that pair back to back, deliberately. It also guards against the predictable error of reaching for że everywhere now that że has just been taught as THE way to attach a clause. MATRIX VERBS ARE CONSTRAINED BY A STANDING QUARANTINE, and this is the unit's real scope limit, logged rather than worked around. a2_directions_func taught wiem as a street phrase and quarantined it ('never conjugates wiem, never shows the infinitive'); b2_ze_clauses held that quarantine and so does this pack. So the openers available are Wiem, Nie wiem (both first person, both owned, nie wiem itself being a taught chunk) and powiedział / powiedziała from b2_reported one node earlier — which is why that unit's new verb is recycled here in three items. wiesz, wie and wiedzieć appear nowhere. The consequence, stated plainly: Dad can say 'I don't know where...' but not 'Do you know where...?', which is the more useful sentence in a street. LIFTING THE QUARANTINE — teaching wiedzieć properly, with the wiedzieć/znać split — is a real unit and belongs on the C1 inbox; it was not smuggled in here because that split is a second system and this unit already has a construction to land. AN IOU CREATED FOR b2_jesli, FLAGGED HERE BECAUSE IT WILL NOT BE OBVIOUS LATER: the classic English-speaker error with czy is confusing it with 'if'-the-condition. That error is IMPOSSIBLE today, because jeśli is verified NEW and is not taught until b2_jesli (two nodes on). So this pack cannot usefully drill the contrast — but b2_jesli arrives holding the other half of it and SHOULD carry the czy/jeśli discrimination, since by then the learner will own both and English will be collapsing them onto one word. THE TWELVE QUESTION WORDS ARE THE MATCH BOARD, one per row: gdzie, kiedy, ile, czy, dlaczego, który, kto, co, kogo, kim, czym, komu. Five of those (kogo, kim, czym, komu, plus czego held back) came from b2_kim_czym five nodes ago, which is why this unit can afford a full board without teaching anything: it is the first place the oblique question words get used for real rather than in isolation, and b2_kim_czym fenced embedded questions absolutely for exactly this reason. FENCED: wiesz / wie / wiedzieć / pamiętam (all verified NEW, pamiętam being the obvious second matrix verb and simply not owned); jeśli (NEW, b2_jesli's); czego, held back although b2_kim_czym taught it, because its natural home is szukać + Genitive and this pack does not want to import a governor to fill one board row; question words followed by an infinitive (nie wiem, co robić), which is a separate construction and a second fact; masculine-ANIMATE relative pronouns, b2_ktory_full's material on the very next node, so który appears here only as an interrogative inside the embedded question (Nie wiem, który film jest dobry), never as a relative pointing back at an antecedent; plural past of powiedzieć, held from b2_reported. otwarty and zamknięty are used as the PLAIN ADJECTIVES leaf_shopping_a1 taught them as, NOT as the passive participles b2_participle_pass will later reveal them to be — same care b2_ze_clauses took with zamknięty. Distractors are real taught Polish in the wrong slot throughout: every wrong choice is że, żeby, czy or one of the owned question words, placed where the meaning does not license it. Nothing fabricated.

nodes.label: Film, o którym…
nodes.label_en: Pointing back with który, after a preposition
nodes.note: B2 Block 4, unit 5 (spine). PAYS B1-DIGEST DEFERRED ITEM #2, both halves at once, which is why the spine put it here rather than at B1. HALF (a): Locative and Instrumental relatives. b1_ktory_cases fenced these completely and its own note logged them as 'deferred to a later pass or a dedicated unit'. This is that unit. Governors are the three already owned and each keeps the case it has always had — o + Locative (a2_o_loc), z + Instrumental (a2_inst_z), w + Locative (a1_prep_w_loc) — plus the bare Instrumental of transport (a2_inst_transport, autobus, którym jadę). Nothing about the prepositions changes. HALF (b): masculine-ANIMATE antecedents. b1_ktory_cases fenced them and said exactly why: którego would then sit in the Accusative table for a DIFFERENT reason than in the Genitive table. That objection has since dissolved — b2_adj_gen taught Accusative-equals-Genitive for masculine animates as a general fact, and AGENTS.md names it as the honest exception. So pies, którego mam is now a re-sighting, not a new rule, and the pack says so. ONE NEW STRING IN THE WHOLE UNIT: którym. której, którą and którego are all already owned and are extended to new jobs — the course's signature 'same endings, another job' idiom, and this is its fifth turn (inst_identity → inst_z → inst_transport, then adj_loc → adj_inst, then pron_prep, then question_cases, now this). THE GIFT, and it is the reason slide 4 exists: every merger this unit needs has already been met, three or four times over. którym covers Locative and Instrumental exactly as dobrym does (adj_loc → adj_inst), as nim does (pron_prep) and as kim does (question_cases). której covers Genitive and Locative exactly as dobrej and niej do. którą covers Accusative and Instrumental exactly as dobrą and nią do. którego covers Genitive and Accusative-animate exactly as dobrego and kogo do. The learner is not being asked to absorb a fourth pattern; he is being shown that the pattern he already has reaches one more word. THE HOMOGRAPH TRAP IS LIVE AND IS NAMED OUT LOUD ON SLIDE 2, and it is the sharpest one this level has hit. o której is a FROZEN CHUNK the learner has owned since a2_ordinals_time, where it means 'at what time' (O której jest spotkanie?). The relative o której — książka, o której mówiłem — is the same two strings doing an entirely unrelated job. check_new.py reports której as TAUGHT and names a2_ordinals_time as the owner, exactly the reporting AGENTS.md's homograph section warns must be read rather than skimmed. It gets a named line and quiz item 12 puts the frozen chunk directly beside the relative, the ci/ci and może/może treatment. Note b1_ktory_cases already did half this work, re-teaching której as a Genitive; this unit is the second time the same string has been re-opened, and the pack says that too. THE ANIMACY CONTRAST IS THE OTHER DISCRIMINATION and it is drilled as a pair: film, który oglądałem versus pies, którego mam. Same job in the sentence, different shape, and the only thing deciding it is whether the thing pointed at is alive. Quiz items 6, 7 and 8 carry it. FENCED, deliberately and all verified NEW: ALL PLURAL RELATIVES — którzy, których, którymi and the plural którym — because plural oblique adjectives are B2-SPINE O3's explicit hand-over to C1 and the relative pronoun declines like an adjective, so shipping plural relatives here would breach that fence by the back door; któremu, the DATIVE relative, which is a fifth case and a fifth new string in a unit that already has four jobs to land, and which mirrors b2_pron_prep's decision to fence niemu — logged as a scope cut, not an oversight, and it belongs on the C1 inbox beside the plural forms; kolegę and filmie, both verified NEW, which killed two otherwise-natural sentences during drafting (Znam kolegę, z którym pracujesz and Mama mówi o filmie) and were replaced rather than smuggled in; dla (verified NEW, dropped from b2_pron_prep for the same reason); negated objects anywhere, since Nie znam filmu needs the Genitive of negation, which is b2_neg_gen's job later in B2; siebie / sobie (C1, spine O15). EVERY ANTECEDENT IS A NOUN THE LEARNER OWNS and every verb inside every relative clause is owned too, so the only thing to work out in any item is the shape of the one pronoun. mówiłem is glossed 'was talking about' throughout, per AGENTS.md's dynamic-verb rule — which reads naturally here, unlike in a reporting frame. QUIZ ANSWER REPEATS ARE DELIBERATE, the b2_kim_czym and b2_ze_clauses reasoning: a unit about the forms of ONE pronoun has five legal answer strings in total. Five distinct answers across twelve items, every prompt distinct, and the repeats sit under different genders, different governors and different cases. Distractors are the other forms of który taught or owned at this point, placed where the gender or the case does not license them. Nothing fabricated anywhere.

nodes.label: Powód i cel
nodes.note: B2 Block 4 vocab (spine). TWELVE NEW WORDS, all verified NEW: przyczyna, skutek, wpływ, zmiana, rozwiązanie, wada, zaleta, cel, sposób, możliwość, wybór, decyzja. The spine offered sixteen and said trim to twelve; korzyść, wartość, społeczeństwo and środowisko were dropped (korzyść duplicates zaleta's gloss and would have been a third soft feminine; the other three are essay words, not opinion words) and handed to the C1 inbox. TAUGHT AS PAIRS because that is how they are used: przyczyna/skutek and wada/zaleta. THREE INFLECTED FORMS taught alongside the citations: przyczynę (feminine accusative) and wady/zalety (feminine plural, which covers Nom and Acc alike for non-virile nouns). wady/zalety carry the -y homograph AGENTS.md names — plural versus genitive singular — so the pack teaches them explicitly as plurals, says so in an explain, and uses them in no other job. możliwość is a soft feminine, badged f and anchored on mysz and noc. sposób, wybór (ó/o alternation) and skutek (fleeting e) appear in the Nominative and Accusative only, where a masculine thing does not move, so their alternations are never met. FENCED: no genitive of any new noun, which cost Nie ma rozwiązania deliberately — b2_health_system already spent one flagged exception on the -e neuter genitive (skierowania) and asked James to rule on it, so this pack does not double down; no locative or dative of any new noun; na + Accusative held out per b2_health_system, which cost mieć wpływ na and is the strongest argument for a na + Accusative unit at C1; ważny fenced (verified NEW, belongs to b2_travel_func); zmienić, jaki, trudny all untaught and kept out.

nodes.label: Jeśli…
nodes.note: B2 Block 4, unit 6 (spine). ONE NEW WORD IN THE ENTIRE UNIT: jeśli, verified NEW. Zero new morphology — both halves of every sentence are tenses the learner already owns, and b2_copular_future back in Block 1 is what makes the natural result clause (będę w parku) expressible at all. THE ONE REAL TEACHING POINT BEYOND THE WORD is the tense inside the jeśli-clause, framed as ENGLISH being the odd one out rather than Polish demanding something extra — the a2_bedzie / b2_indirect_q gift idiom, fourth outing. English uses a present after 'if' even when it plainly means the future; Polish just puts in the tense it means (Jeśli pogoda BĘDZIE ładna, będę w parku). Present-tense conditions stay present (Jeśli masz czas, zrobię obiad), so both tenses are drilled and the choice is always 'what do you actually mean'. Quiz 5 and 6 drill it in recognition; five type items demand it in production and each carries an explain, since the English prompt deliberately does not show it. PAYS b2_indirect_q's EXPLICIT IOU, created there and flagged as one that would not be obvious later: the classic error is confusing czy with jeśli, impossible to drill at the time because jeśli was still untaught, and handed forward to this unit by name. It lands as a minimal pair on ONE clause — quiz 11 Nie wiem, CZY to jest dobra decyzja against quiz 12 JEŚLI to jest dobra decyzja, będzie dobrze — with a test the learner can apply in English: swap 'if' for 'whether' and it is czy; swap it for 'in the case that' and it is jeśli. Both czy sentences are produced, not merely recognised, in Użycie. Second contrast, one item: jeśli against bo. WORD ORDER IS FENCED TO jeśli-FIRST, conservative branch, logged. The reversed order (Będę w parku, jeśli…) is grammatical and common but is a second fact, and every subordinate clause the learner owns so far — że, żeby, który, embedded questions — comes second, so jeśli-first is already the new shape. All twelve match rows share one skeleton on purpose. Reversed order goes to the C1 inbox. FENCED, all verified NEW: jeżeli; gdy; the resumptive to / wtedy in the result clause, a new job for a string this learner reads as 'this' and a poor thing to plant one node before b2_gdyby; and EVERY UNREAL CONDITIONAL, which is b2_gdyby's entire content on the very next node — no by-form appears anywhere, not in a table, not as a distractor, checked by grep rather than by eye. The existential będzie kawa stays fenced per b2_copular_future, so weather conditions are built subject-first (Jeśli pogoda będzie ładna), never the spine's drafted Jeśli będzie ładna pogoda — changed for exactly that reason. otwarty and zamknięty are used as the PLAIN ADJECTIVES leaf_shopping_a1 taught, not as the participles b2_participle_pass later reveals. Recycles b2_abstract from the node immediately before: sposób, decyzja and rozwiązanie all do real work in the result clauses.

nodes.label: Gdybym miał czas…
nodes.note: B2 Block 4, unit 7 (spine). PAYS b1_conditional_sg's NAMED FENCE — that pack allowed 'simple wishes and soft requests only, no gdybym/jeśli…by clauses' — and it sits one node after b2_jesli so real and unreal conditions arrive back to back and are taught against each other. THREE NEW STRINGS AND NOTHING ELSE: gdybym, gdybyś, gdyby. THE PERSON MARKER IS THE THIRD TURN OF ONE PATTERN and the pack says so out loud: -m / -ś / nothing is the identical family already owned as bym/byś/by (b1_conditional_sg) and żebym/żebyś (b1_zeby). THE SHAPE PARALLEL WITH żeby IS THE BEST ANCHOR and is drilled, not merely mentioned — quiz 10 and Użycie 9 both make the learner produce a żeby sentence inside this unit; the skeleton is identical, marker on the function word and a plain L-form on the verb. THE DOUBLE MARKER is named once, on slide 3: in a full sentence -bym surfaces twice, once on gdyby and once on the result verb, which looks like a slip until somebody points at it. THE APODOSIS IS SHARPLY LIMITED BY WHAT b1_conditional_sg ACTUALLY TAUGHT, and this constrained the whole pack, not one sentence: zrobiłbym is verified NEW, so 'I would make dinner' — the most natural sentence in the unit — IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE and appears nowhere. The only owned first-person conditionals are chciałbym/chciałabym and kupiłbym/kupiłabym, so every 1sg result clause is built from those two verbs; third person is much freer, which is why most of the board runs on mama and tata rather than ja. This is a real scope limit and the first thing to look at if the unit feels narrow. REAL AGAINST UNREAL is the discrimination carried forward from b2_jesli as a minimal pair on ONE clause (quiz 1 vs quiz 2), and quiz 9 holds the three-way English collapse open — 'if' is czy, jeśli or gdyby depending on the job, live all at once for the first time. FENCED, all verified NEW: byłbym/byłby — the conditional of być is NOT taught, so 'I would be…' is unavailable and every result clause wanting it was rebuilt around chciałbym być; zrobiłbym, zrobiłabyś, kupiłbyś, miałbym, mógłbym; and poszedłbym, which is the spine's own drafted example for this unit and the third prefix on iść's suppletive stem that b1_wrapup already caught and rejected once. ALL PLURAL gdyby FORMS (gdybyśmy, gdybyście) held, mirroring b1_conditional_sg's and b1_zeby's singular-first splits — C1 inbox. THE CONDITIONAL PAST (byłbym miał) is B2-SPINE O6's deferral to C1, so the L-form after gdyby is glossed ONLY as a present unreal ('if I had time', never 'if I had had time'); that Polish uses one shape for both readings is not mentioned at all rather than half-taught. DISTRACTORS ARE OWNED FORMS IN THE WRONG SLOT throughout. miałby and miałaby are deliberately NOT used anywhere — they would be the sharpest distractors for the plain-L-form fact but are real untaught Polish, and a button would teach the string through the back door; one draft slide spelled miałby in prose and was rewritten. The same fact is drilled from the other side instead, in quiz 5, 6 and 7. mógłby/mogłaby are recycled from b1_polite's 'czy mógłby pan' formula into plain third-person use, which is the same grammatical job in a new frame and is named in an explain.

nodes.label: W domach, w sklepach
nodes.note: B2 Block 5, unit 1 of 7 (spine O9). Locative plural -ach: ONE ending for every gender, no exception among the words this course owns - the smallest thing in the level and placed first in the block for that reason. THE ANCHOR IS A PHRASE ALREADY OWNED: a2_travel taught w gorach as a frozen holiday chunk, so slide 1 opens by pointing at a form Dad has produced since A2 rather than by announcing a new case; gorach is recycled and is the one match row that is not new. ELEVEN NEW FORMS, all verified NEW: domach, sklepach, hotelach, bankach, szkolach, firmach, gazetach, miastach, biurach, mieszkaniach, biurkach - four masculine, four feminine, four neuter counting gorach, because the unit's claim is that gender stops mattering here and the board has to show it. THE RULE IS STATED IN THE FORM IT IS ACTUALLY TRUE IN: not 'add -ach to the plural' and not 'add -ach to the Locative singular' (w miescie -> w miastach kills both), but 'take the plain dictionary word, drop a final vowel if there is one, add -ach'. THE HOMOGRAPH DECISION SHAPED THE WHOLE PACK: the obvious table pairs the nominative plural with the new form (szkoly -> szkolach) and is WRONG - szkoly reports TAUGHT but its owners are a1_gen_endings and a1_prep_do_z, where it is the GENITIVE SINGULAR (ze szkoly). Same trap on miasta, ksiazki, biura and firmy, every one owned as a genitive singular and none as a nominative plural. So the left column is the LOCATIVE SINGULAR he really owns (w szkole, w miescie, w biurze, w firmie), and the honestly-owned nominative plurals (sklepy, banki, hotele, domy, okna, telefony, klucze) are used only as sentence subjects. THE PREDICTABLE ERROR IS THE GENITIVE PLURAL, not the singular: a2_gen_pl taught domow, sklepow, bankow, gazet, miast, biur next to duzo, blisko and nie ma, so slide 4 and four quiz items hold duzo sklepow apart from w sklepach. QUIZ ITEM 1 IS DELIBERATELY NOT THIS LESSON'S FORM - the answer is domu with domach on the button row - because a unit whose every answer is the new ending teaches button-picking. FENCED: no plural adjectives of any kind (spine O3 -> C1), which makes this an entirely bare-noun unit; gor, szkol, firm (verified NEW), so only a2_gen_pl's own word list appears in the duzo contrast; oknie, mieszkania, biurka, restauracje, komputery, tych, moi, wiele, all verified NEW; and dzieciach/ludziach, regular and legal but held back because those two nouns head the irregular INSTRUMENTAL plurals b2_inst_pl must rule on one node later - dzieci and ludzie appear as subjects only.

nodes.label: Z rodzicami
nodes.note: B2 Block 5, unit 2 of 7 (spine O9). Instrumental plural -ami, drilled in ONE owned job: companionship after z. PAYS a2_inst_z's NAMED FENCE, which reads 'plural instrumental (z rodzicami, z dziecmi) - B1, different ending set' - it named both phrases, so both are paid rather than half. ONE JOB ONLY, DELIBERATELY: the Instrumental has three owned duties (identity jestem studentem, companionship z bratem, transport jade autobusem) and only companionship gets a plural today, mirroring a2_inst_z's own 'deliberately ONE new thing' framing; jestesmy studentami is a logged, cost-free top-up if the unit plays thin. TWELVE NEW FORMS, all verified NEW: rodzicami, dziecmi, kolegami, siostrami, corkami, synami, bracmi, ludzmi, klientami, pacjentami, kotami, ciociami. THE ANCHOR IS a2_inst_z's OWN BOARD - five of its twelve singulars return as the intro's left column (z synem, z kolega, z siostra, z corka, z ciocia), so slide 1 shows -em and -a alike collapsing into one plural ending. Slide 3 pairs the unit against b2_loc_pl one node earlier: -ach after w/na/o, -ami after z, the little word deciding - which is why the two are adjacent, and gorach/domach/szkolach are recycled straight across. THREE WORDS REFUSE, taking -mi: dziecmi, bracmi, ludzmi, handed over whole in one marked box. BRACMI IS A DELIBERATE EXTENSION BEYOND THE SPINE'S LIST, which named only dziecmi/ludzmi: a2_inst_z made z bratem the FIRST item on its board, so brat is the noun Dad has produced most often in exactly this construction, and teaching -ami while leaving it alone hands him a wrong form he has every reason to build. NO NON-WORD IS EVER PRINTED - slide 4 says brat 'does not simply add -ami' rather than spelling out the fabrication, and no choice list contains an invented string. DISTRACTORS: where four owned forms of a noun exist the list is that noun's own paradigm (bracmi/bratem/brat/brata; dziecmi/dzieckiem/dziecko/dzieci; kotami/koty/kota/kotow; corkami/corka/corki/corka); where only three exist the fourth button is another noun's REAL -ami form in the wrong meaning and the explain says so. ze IS VERIFIED NEW AND SHAPED THE WORD LIST: ze studentami was the natural 'with students' row, but a1_prep_do_z taught only the chunks ze szkoly / ze sklepu and never the bare preposition, so studentami was dropped and klientami/pacjentami took its place - all twelve rows take plain z. FENCED, all verified NEW: przyjaciolmi and goscmi (a fourth and fifth exception would turn a marked box into a paradigm); lekarzami, nauczycielami - those nouns appear as SUBJECTS only; bracia, synowie, siostry, ciocie, kolegi, syna, cioci, klienta, pacjenta, kotem, czlowiek, so ludzie is handed over with no singular anchor at all and slide 4 says so; rozmawiam/rozmawia; razem, spotykam, w pilke, na wakacje. NO DATIVE PLURAL of any kind - rodzicom, dzieciom, ludziom are b2_dat_pl's entire content on the very next node and appear nowhere, not as a distractor. No plural adjectives (spine O3 -> C1), so the unit is bare-noun throughout like b2_loc_pl.

nodes.label: Studentom, rodzicom
nodes.note: B2 Block 5, unit 3 of 7 (spine O9) - the plural-oblique strand closes. Dative plural -om: one ending, no gender split, no exception among the words used; the spine calls it 'deliberately small' and it is. THE UNIT RUNS ON THE SAME TWELVE NOUNS AS b2_inst_pl, IN THE SAME ORDER, which is the design: one fixed cast takes three different endings on three consecutive nodes (w domach, z rodzicami, pomagam rodzicom), so the plural obliques read as one table with three columns rather than three unrelated word lists. TWELVE NEW FORMS, all verified NEW: rodzicom, dzieciom, ludziom, studentom, kolegom, siostrom, corkom, synom, klientom, pacjentom, kotom, ciociom. THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE HARD PART IS BEHIND HIM - b1_dative_sg had to teach its singular endings one word at a time (mamie, tacie, siostrze, studentowi, nauczycielowi) because the dative singular genuinely is unpredictable, and the plural is a single -om for all of it. HOW THE FORM IS BUILT IS STATED FROM LAST LESSON'S FORM, not the dictionary word, because that is what is reliable here: nine of the twelve are b2_inst_pl's -ami with -om in its place. The 'drop a final vowel' rule that served the two previous units BREAKS on dzieci, whose final -i belongs to the stem, so dzieci and ludzie get their own slide rather than being forced into the general rule. SLIDE 3 IS THE PAYOFF FOR LAST LESSON'S EXCEPTION BOX: dziecko and ludzie took -mi there and had to be learned whole, and here they are ordinary - with the useful part said out loud, that they must be built from the plain words dzieci/ludzie and NOT from dziecmi/ludzmi, which is the mistake the previous unit sets up. BRAT IS ABSENT BY DESIGN AND IS THE UNIT'S ONE REAL GAP: braciom is verified NEW and cannot be reached from brat by any rule this course has stated (it needs the braci- plural stem). b2_inst_pl deliberately taught bracmi one node back; the same argument would justify braciom, but this unit's whole claim is 'one ending, nothing to learn whole'. The word appears nowhere in the pack in any form - a first draft quoted the owned dative SINGULAR bratu on slide 1 and it was cut, because naming the word invites a learner to reach for its plural.
